overall: The AG found the Leicester School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by approving July 6 minutes late and by approving executive session minutes too thin to convey the discussion; it ordered revised minutes certified within 60 days.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the Committee failed to timely approve the open and executive session minutes of its July 6 meeting until September 15.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee concedes that it failed to timely approve these minutes as the minutes were not approved until September 15, which was not within the later of the next three meetings or 30 days following the July 6 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the July 6 executive session minutes lacked an adequate summary of the one-hour contract-negotiation discussion, even after an October 4 revision.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the minutes do not adequately capture the substance of the discussions that occurred so that a member of the public who did not attend the meeting could read the minutes and have an understanding of what occurred.

remedy: Revise the July 6 executive session meeting minutes and certify to the AG's office within sixty (60) days of the letter that this was done.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee to revise the July 6 executive session meeting minutes and to certify to this office within sixty (60) days of the date of this letter that it has done so.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
